answer: An archive of tundra maps and marble scans could require each earning key to store a separately encoded data replica. Validators demand proofs for unpredictable byte ranges under a short deadline and suspend keys that fail; sound proofs are costly to forge without the replica. Every added alias needs more disk space and audit bandwidth, even in a parallel farm. This assumes secure encoding and deadlines too short to regenerate missing data. Outsourcing still costs money; honest newcomers need storage, and encoding flaws could let attackers reuse space.
